name: ResiSolve
project:
Each organization represents a property management company. The company can create buildings, units, and maintenance service categories. Some categories can remain as drafts or inactive.

On the tenant route, residents can view active service categories, submit maintenance requests, and see only their own requests. On the organization route, staff can manage properties, requests, statuses, and assignments.

This tests multi-tenant isolation, tenant-specific routes, scopes, and authorization policies.
description: Multi-tenant property management platform streamlining maintenance requests and resident communications.

current_prd.elevator_pitch: For property management companies struggling with chaotic maintenance tracking and disconnected resident communication, ResiSolve is a multi-tenant platform that centralizes property operations. Unlike generic ticketing systems, ResiSolve provides strict organizational isolation, allowing staff to easily manage buildings, units, and service categories, manually onboard tenants, and assign requests to internal technicians. With real-time, in-app comment threads on every maintenance ticket, ResiSolve ensures transparent, efficient communication that reduces vacancy downtime and boosts resident satisfaction.
current_prd.problem_statement: Property management companies often struggle to manage maintenance requests efficiently across multiple buildings and units. Communication between residents and staff is frequently fragmented across emails, phone calls, and texts, leading to delayed responses, lost requests, and frustrated tenants. Additionally, existing solutions lack strict multi-tenant isolation, making it difficult for management companies to securely isolate data, manage custom service categories, onboard tenants securely, and coordinate manual technician assignments in a single, unified system.
current_prd.solution: ResiSolve solves these challenges by providing a secure, multi-tenant property management and maintenance platform. Each property management company operates within a strictly isolated organization. Staff members have flat permissions to manage buildings, units, and service categories (active, draft, inactive), manually onboard tenants with temporary passwords, and assign requests to internal technicians. Residents can easily submit maintenance requests under active categories, track progress, and communicate directly with staff via an in-app comment thread on the specific request, ensuring all communication is centralized and transparent.

key_features.feature_description: Strict data isolation at the database and API levels, ensuring each property management company (organization) can only access its own buildings, units, staff, tenants, and maintenance data.
Comprehensive back-office tools for Property Staff to create, update, and delete buildings and individual units within their organization.
Ability for Property Staff to define and manage maintenance service categories (e.g., Plumbing, Electrical, HVAC) with states: Active, Draft, or Inactive.
Staff-initiated tenant creation where Property Staff manually input tenant details, link them to a specific building and unit, and generate a secure temporary password for initial login.
Residents can view active service categories, submit detailed maintenance requests (with description and severity), and track the real-time status of their own requests.
A real-time, centralized communication thread on each maintenance request page, allowing Residents and Property Staff to exchange messages, updates, and clarifications.
Flat-permission workflow allowing any Property Staff member to manually assign maintenance requests to specific internal technicians and update request statuses.
Secure JWT-based authentication, role-based access control (RBAC) enforcing flat staff permissions, and comprehensive API logging for audit trails.

current_prd.success_metrics:
- **Time to Resolution (TTR):** 30% reduction in average time from maintenance request submission to completion.
- **Resident Satisfaction (CSAT):** Achieve and maintain a CSAT score of 4.5/5 or higher for maintenance handling.
- **Platform Adoption:** 90%+ of residents onboarded by staff successfully log in and submit requests through the platform.
- **Operational Efficiency:** 40% reduction in inbound phone calls and emails regarding maintenance updates due to the in-app comment thread.
- **Tenant Retention:** 15% increase in tenant lease renewals correlated with improved maintenance response times.
current_prd.competitors:
- **AppFolio:** A comprehensive property management software, but can be overly complex and expensive for mid-sized companies wanting a focused maintenance workflow.
- **Propertyware:** Offers robust property management but lacks a modern, streamlined, real-time in-app communication thread specifically optimized for rapid maintenance resolution.
- **TenantCloud:** Provides basic tenant and maintenance tracking, but lacks strict multi-tenant organizational isolation and flexible service category states (active/draft/inactive) tailored for custom staff workflows.
current_prd.vision: To become the industry-standard maintenance and operations operating system for property management companies globally, fostering seamless, transparent, and high-trust relationships between residents, property staff, and technicians through modern, intuitive, and secure software.

phasing.rationale: Establishes the secure multi-tenant foundation, JWT authentication, and database/API isolation required before any property or user data is created.

Allows property staff to set up the physical infrastructure (buildings, units) and service categories (Plumbing, Electrical, etc.) that are prerequisites for onboarding tenants and submitting requests.
Enables staff to onboard tenants with temporary passwords, and allows tenants to log in, reset their password, and submit maintenance requests against active categories.
Completes the lifecycle by allowing staff to assign requests to technicians and enabling real-time, in-app comment threads between tenants and staff.

current_prd.design_principles:
### ResiSolve Core Design Principles

1. **Mobile-First & Responsive Design**
   - **Context**: Residents primarily access the platform via mobile devices while experiencing active maintenance issues. Staff and technicians require on-the-go access while walking properties or performing repairs.
   - **Execution**: All layouts are designed starting from a 375px viewport width, utilizing fluid grids, touch-friendly targets (minimum 44x44px), and collapsible navigation. Desktop layouts expand gracefully to provide dense, multi-column data views for back-office staff.

2. **Clear Status Indicators & Visual Hierarchy**
   - **Context**: Maintenance requests progress through distinct lifecycle stages (Submitted, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved, Cancelled). Users must understand status at a glance without reading dense text.
   - **Execution**: Standardized, high-contrast color-coded badges are used across both portals:
     - *Submitted*: Blue (`#2563EB`) - indicates a new request awaiting review.
     - *Assigned*: Purple (`#7C3AED`) - indicates a technician has been assigned.
     - *In Progress*: Amber (`#D97706`) - indicates active work is underway.
     - *Resolved*: Green (`#059669`) - indicates successful completion.
     - *Cancelled*: Gray (`#4B5563`) - indicates the request was retracted or closed without action.
   - Status badges are consistently positioned in the top-right of request cards and detail headers.

3. **High Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance)**
   - **Context**: ResiSolve is a multi-tenant utility platform that must be usable by all residents, including those with visual, motor, or cognitive impairments.
   - **Execution**: 
     - Minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.
     - Full keyboard navigability with highly visible focus rings (`#2563EB` outline with offset).
     - Semantic HTML structure with appropriate ARIA labels for dynamic elements (e.g., comment threads, status dropdowns).
     - Screen-reader friendly status updates (using `aria-live="polite"` for real-time comment additions).

4. **Clean Multi-Tenant Separation & Trust**
   - **Context**: ResiSolve hosts multiple property management organizations. It is critical that staff and residents never see data, branding, or units belonging to another organization.
   - **Execution**: 
     - Clear organization branding (logo and primary color accent) dynamically loaded in the header.
     - Explicit breadcrumbs and page titles that reinforce the current building and unit context (e.g., "Oakridge Apartments > Unit 402").
     - Strict visual isolation: no cross-tenant search results, suggestions, or shared directories are ever exposed in the UI.

- Login (/login) - Secure entry point for all users (residents, staff, and technicians).

current_prd.navigation_design:
### ResiSolve Navigation Design & Patterns

ResiSolve employs distinct navigation patterns tailored to the primary devices and workflows of its two main user groups: Residents (mobile-first, task-focused) and Property Staff (desktop-first, management-focused).

---

#### 1. Resident (Tenant) Portal Navigation
The Resident Portal is optimized for mobile screens to ensure quick, frictionless submission and tracking of maintenance requests.

*   **Primary Navigation Pattern**: **Bottom Navigation Bar (Mobile)** & **Top Header Navigation (Desktop)**
    *   **Bottom Navigation Bar (Mobile)**: Fixed to the bottom of the viewport on mobile devices for easy thumb reach.
        *   *Home/Dashboard* (`/tenant/dashboard`): Icon of a house. Directs to the main dashboard.
        *   *My Requests* (`/tenant/requests`): Icon of a list/clipboard. Directs to the request history.
        *   *New Request* (`/tenant/requests/new`): Prominent, floating action button (FAB) styled in the center of the bottom bar with a plus (`+`) icon, highlighted in the organization's primary brand color.
    *   **Top Header Navigation (Desktop)**: Standard horizontal bar containing:
        *   Organization Logo (left-aligned, links to `/tenant/dashboard`).
        *   Text links: "Dashboard", "My Requests", and a "New Request" button.
        *   User Profile Dropdown (right-aligned) containing "Reset Password" (`/reset-password`) and "Logout".
*   **Contextual Navigation**:
    *   **Back Button**: Present in the top-left header of `/tenant/requests/new` and `/tenant/requests/:id` to return the user to the previous screen without losing state.
    *   **Breadcrumbs**: Displayed on desktop viewports above the page title (e.g., `Home > My Requests > Request #1024`).

---

#### 2. Property Staff Portal Navigation
The Staff Portal is designed for high-density data management, multitasking, and rapid navigation between queues, properties, and tenant records.

*   **Primary Navigation Pattern**: **Collapsible Left Sidebar (Desktop/Tablet)** & **Hamburger Menu (Mobile)**
    *   **Left Sidebar (Desktop)**: A persistent, dark-themed sidebar that can be collapsed to an icon-only view to maximize screen real estate for large tables.
        *   *Dashboard* (`/staff/dashboard`): Icon of a dashboard/grid. Central queue of all requests.
        *   *Tenants* (`/staff/tenants`): Icon of users. Tenant directory and onboarding.
        *   *Properties* (`/staff/properties`): Icon of a building. Property and unit configuration.
        *   *Categories* (`/staff/categories`): Icon of tags/settings. Service category lifecycle management.
    *   **Sidebar Footer**:
        *   User Profile Card showing Sarah's name, role ("Property Staff"), and an arrow icon opening a menu with "Reset Password" (`/reset-password`) and "Logout".
    *   **Hamburger Menu (Mobile/Tablet)**: On smaller screens, the sidebar collapses into a standard hamburger icon in the top-left of the header. Tapping it slides the full menu in from the left.
*   **Contextual Navigation**:
    *   **Tabs on Request Details** (`/staff/requests/:id`):
        *   *Details Tab*: Shows request description, severity, and technician assignment dropdown.
        *   *Activity & Comments Tab*: Displays the real-time comment thread and system audit logs.
    *   **Global Search & Filters**: A persistent top bar on `/staff/dashboard` allows staff to instantly filter the request queue by Building, Status, or Severity, and search by Tenant Name or Request ID.

user_stories.title: Multi-Tenant Data Isolation

user_story.i_want: the system to strictly isolate my organization's data
user_story.so_that: I cannot view or modify buildings, units, tenants, or requests belonging to other organizations

acceptance_criteria: Only property_staff can access /staff/dashboard
All database queries for buildings, units, and requests must filter by the authenticated user's organization_id
API requests attempting to access resources with an organization_id other than the user's token organization_id must return a 403 Forbidden error
Only property_staff can access /staff/properties

user_stories.title: Create and Manage Buildings

user_story.i_want: to create and manage buildings within my organization
user_story.so_that: I can organize units and tenants under specific physical properties

acceptance_criteria: Only property_staff can access /staff/properties
Staff can create a building by providing a name, address, and total floors
System validates that building name and address are not empty, displaying validation errors if they are
Newly created buildings are immediately visible in the properties list and associated with the staff's organization
The data model stores last name and the application uses it as described in this story.

user_stories.title: Create and Manage Units

user_story.i_want: to add individual units to a specific building
user_story.so_that: I can assign tenants and maintenance requests to specific physical locations

acceptance_criteria: Only property_staff can access /staff/properties/:building_id/units
Staff can add a unit by specifying a unit number, floor, and optional notes
System prevents duplicate unit numbers within the same building and displays an error message
Units are successfully saved and linked to the parent building in the database

user_stories.title: Service Category Lifecycle Management

user_story.i_want: to create and manage maintenance service categories with active, draft, or inactive states
user_story.so_that: I can control which categories are available for tenants to select when submitting requests

acceptance_criteria: Only property_staff can access /staff/categories
Staff can create a category with a name, description, and initial status set to 'Draft'
Staff can update a category's status to 'Active' or 'Inactive'
Only categories with 'Active' status are visible to tenants when submitting a request
System validates that category name is unique within the organization

user_stories.title: Tenant Onboarding by Staff

user_story.i_want: to manually create tenant accounts, link them to a building and unit, and generate a temporary password
user_story.so_that: tenants can securely log in for the first time

acceptance_criteria: Only property_staff can access /staff/tenants
Staff can create a tenant by entering name, email, phone, and selecting an existing building and unit
System generates a secure temporary password and displays it to the staff member to copy
System saves the tenant record with a flag indicating that a password reset is required on first login
System prevents creating a tenant with an email that already exists in the system

user_stories.title: First-Time Tenant Login & Password Reset

user_story.i_want: to log in with my temporary password and be forced to set a new secure password
user_story.so_that: my account is secure and I can access the tenant dashboard

Upon successful password reset, the temporary password flag is cleared, and the tenant is redirected to /tenant/dashboard

user_stories.title: Maintenance Request Submission

user_story.so_that: property staff can address the issue in my unit

current_prd.industry_category: Real Estate Technology / Property Management Software
current_prd.tam_description: Total Addressable Market for the North American Property Management Software Market, encompassing all software solutions used by property management companies for various operations, including accounting, leasing, maintenance, and tenant communication.
current_prd.tam_estimation_basis: Top-down approach based on the estimated total market size of property management software in North America.
current_prd.tam_source: Simulated data based on industry reports from Grand View Research, Statista, and similar market analysis firms for the North American Property Management Software Market (2023-2027 estimates).
current_prd.sam_description: Serviceable Available Market for Mid-Sized Property Management Operations & Maintenance Software in North America. This segment focuses on property management companies that require robust, multi-tenant solutions for maintenance tracking, resident communication, and core property operations, but find enterprise solutions overly complex or expensive, and basic tools insufficient.
current_prd.sam_estimation_basis: Estimated 30% of the total TAM, representing the segment of mid-sized property management companies that are the primary target for ResiSolve's focused maintenance and operations platform. This segment is less served by either very large or very small competitors.
current_prd.sam_source: Simulated data based on analysis of property management company size distribution and their specific software needs, as well as competitive landscape segmentation.
current_prd.som_description: Serviceable Obtainable Market, representing the realistic market share ResiSolve can capture within the North American Mid-Sized Property Management Operations & Maintenance Software Market over a 5-year horizon.
current_prd.som_estimation_basis: A conservative 2.5% market penetration rate of the SAM over a 5-year period, considering ResiSolve's competitive advantages and the typical adoption curve for new SaaS solutions in a competitive market.
current_prd.som_source: Simulated data based on typical market entry success rates for SaaS products and competitive analysis of the property management software sector.
current_prd.customer_type: Property management companies (paying customer) and their staff/residents (users)
current_prd.pricing_model_basis: Subscription-based per property management organization, potentially tiered by number of units managed or active staff users.
current_prd.advantage_summary: ResiSolve offers strict multi-tenant organizational isolation, centralized property operations with a strong focus on maintenance, real-time in-app comment threads for transparent communication, flexible service category lifecycle management, and secure manual tenant onboarding and technician assignment. This provides a streamlined, modern, and secure alternative to overly complex enterprise solutions or basic, un-isolated tools, particularly for mid-sized property management companies.
current_prd.project_manager_reasoning: The project definition is exceptionally complete and detailed. All high-priority fields (Problem Statement, Key Features, Target Audience, Vision) are thoroughly developed with realistic, project-specific content. Medium and low-priority fields like User Flows, Competitors, and Success Metrics are also fully fleshed out, providing a clear and comprehensive foundation for the ResiSolve platform.
current_prd.designer_reasoning: The design document is outstanding. It features highly detailed design principles (including specific color codes and WCAG compliance details), three distinct and relevant user personas, comprehensive user journeys, a fully structured sitemap with metadata, and a very thorough navigation design tailored to different user roles and devices.
current_prd.architect_reasoning: The data model is highly comprehensive and robust. The Mermaid ERD diagram clearly defines all necessary entities and relationships for a multi-tenant property management system, including strict organization isolation. The sample data is extensive, realistic, and perfectly aligns with the ERD schema.
current_prd.product_manager_reasoning: The user stories are exemplary. There are 12 highly detailed stories covering all core features of the platform across different phases. Each story includes well-defined roles, goals, benefits, and comprehensive, testable acceptance criteria, far exceeding the minimum requirements.
